notes: ACCESS: same as bs83.json - Akamai blocks direct HTTP/headless Playwright on /shop/, /clearance/, /nextsale paths; used Claude-in-Chrome (tier-3 last resort) for the whole session, no Claude-specific robots.txt disallow. That hub page has TWO distinct sections: an upper 'SALE' section (generic department tiles, no explicit permanence signal) and a lower section explicitly headed 'CLEARANCE' / 'FURTHER REDUCTIONS - MOST ITEMS HALF PRICE OR LESS*' containing per-department tiles including a tile literally labelled 'HOME CLEARANCE' (description: 'A huge variety of stunning items are still available so don't miss out. Shop our home and furniture offers.'). Followed that tile (not the generic Sale one) since the site's own on-page heading and tile copy explicitly use the word 'Clearance', satisfying the brief's Clearance-vs-Sale test. The tile links to /clearance/search?w=homeware&af=department:homeware, a genuine filterable PLP (path itself under /clearance/, 'Search Clearance' facet section, Department/Category/Brand/Colour/Size/Type filters) showing markdown pricing (e.g. was £1,699 now £849). Site's 'Home' department taxonomy includes furniture/garden alongside home accessories (same as the New Arrivals listing), so this single Clearance listing spans that same combined scope - consistent with how Next itself defines 'Home'. No separate homeware-only vs furniture-only Clearance child pages were found (one flat listing with in-page filters, not distinct child URLs), so emitted as a single row rather than a group+children.
